::: {#thm-bayes-posterior}
#### Bayes' theorem for parameters

If $\p(\vy) > 0$, then

$$
\p(\theta \mid \vy)
=
\frac{\p(\vy \mid \theta)\, \p(\theta)}{\p(\vy)}.
$$ {#eq-bayes-posterior}
:::

::: proof
By the definition of a conditional density,
$\p(\theta \mid \vy) = \p(\theta, \vy) / \p(\vy)$
and $\p(\theta, \vy) = \p(\vy \mid \theta)\, \p(\theta)$,
where $\p(\vy)$ is the marginal density of $\vY$ at $\vy$.
That marginal density is

$$
\ba
\p(\vy)
&= \int \p(\theta, \vy)\, d\theta
&& \text{(marginalizing over $\theta$)}\\
&= \int \p(\vy \mid \theta)\, \p(\theta)\, d\theta
&& \text{(substituting the factorization of $\p(\theta, \vy)$)},
\ea
$$

which is the [marginal likelihood](#def-marginal-likelihood).
Substituting the factorization into the numerator of $\p(\theta, \vy) / \p(\vy)$
gives @eq-bayes-posterior.
:::
